prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using bifunctional and molecular-glue small molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to selected proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a genuine new chemical principle: a designed small molecule brings an E3 ligase and a target into one ternary complex and turns occupancy-driven inhibition into event-driven, catalytic removal. The concept (Sakamoto, Crews and Deshaies, 2001) was followed by cell-permeable PROTACs and by structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex design, so the mechanism rests on determined structures, which is the evidence I look for. It has been reproduced by many independent groups across target classes, and several degraders are in clinical trials. I moved B056 to my preferred configuration after reading the openings: four members ranked it first and six ranked it in the top three, and my own B059 case, though scientifically solid, had no support from any colleague.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet an approved drug, so part of the translational case is prospective. The molecular-glue strand (thalidomide and cereblon, Handa and Ito) has a separate history, so a three-person prize built on PROTACs leaves out a defensible discovery and invites a priority dispute between the two strands. My own preference, zeolite and molecular-sieve design (B059), is mature and industrially deployed, but its credit is spread over many groups and it may look diffuse next to a single clear concept.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, arguing that cereblon identification underpins the molecular-glue branch and the CRBN-recruiting degraders.
responses.response: Handa's cereblon work is important, but it explains a drug class that was already clinical, whereas the PROTAC strand defined a design principle that others could apply to any target. If the committee wants Handa, it must say whether the citation covers both strands, and then Ciulli's structural basis for VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity would be the name displaced. I would keep Ciulli, because the structural work is what moved PROTACs from peptidic proofs of concept to drug-like molecules, but I accept this is a real trade-off and not settled by opening support.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B056 first, sees a simple chemical idea opening a new drug modality, and credits Ciulli with the structural basis that made degraders drug-like.
responses.response: I agree with the Ciulli attribution and with the mechanistic clarity. Where I would press harder than Aqvist is that clinical proof is still arriving, so the citation should rest on the chemical concept and the demonstrated mechanism, not on promised therapies. He also ranks genetic-code expansion (B017) second; that is mature and stable, but I find the attribution there less crisp, since Schultz, Wang and Chin each own a different step.

responses.point: Sparr puts phase separation (B024) first, calling it a new thermodynamic description of cell organisation, while noting that in vivo functional relevance is still debated.
responses.response: I respect the conceptual reach, but her own maturity caveat is the one that worries me: it is hard to separate functional condensates from demixing, and the structural evidence for mechanism is thin compared with PROTAC ternary complexes. I would not support B024 as a first choice yet. I do agree with her that the credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is a real choice, and that choice is not fully resolved.

responses.point: Linke ranks perovskites (B068) second and stresses fast efficiency gains, but flags that operational stability, lead toxicity and scale-up leave the technology immature.
responses.response: We agree on the science and on his maturity concern, which is why I hold B068 as an alternative and not as my preferred prize. Where I qualify his view is that the structure and defect chemistry of perovskites is not itself in doubt; the open issue is device lifetime, which is an engineering question the committee has weighed differently in the past. The credit also remains contested beyond Miyasaka, Park and Snaith, with Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B051) first as a general, mature, widely adopted method, with Buchwald and Hartwig as the fair pair.
responses.response: The adoption and ligand design are impressive, but I ranked it low because of the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize, which already honoured the core of the area; a second prize needs an argument that C-N coupling is a distinct principle and not a refinement. I would like to hear that argument, since Somfai knows the synthetic literature better than I do.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks nitrogenase (B060) first for its structural and mechanistic insight into FeMo-cofactor, with Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt as the core.
responses.response: As a structural chemist I find the atomic-resolution case for the interstitial carbide strong, and the structural evidence is better than in most candidates. My hesitation is that the catalytic cycle and substrate-binding state are still unresolved, as he acknowledges, so the prize would honour structure more than mechanism. I would keep it as a credible candidate for later years but not as this year's prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to include the cereblon and molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito), and if so which of Ciulli or Deshaies would be displaced under the three-person limit.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader makes B056 premature this year.
Whether the credit in B056 should reach Sakamoto, who is a co-author of the 2001 PROTAC paper.
Whether zeolite and molecular-sieve design (B059) can be framed as one clear achievement with three names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B056. I work on zeolites and porous framework materials and have a broad network in that field, so I would flag possible professional familiarity with candidates in B059 (for example Jihong Yu and Michael Tsapatsis) and recuse from deciding on that ballot if it advances. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, Peter Brzezinski, which is not a conflict for any shortlisted candidate.
